Intermate x SAMY – Shaping the State of Social

Stellenanforderungen

  • Du zeichnest dich durch hohe Eigenmotivation und Lernbereitschaft aus, strukturierst dich und deine Aufgaben selbstständig und behältst auch in dynamischen Phasen stets den Überblick

jobs.title: SEO Manager (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
About the Job

We're looking for an SEO Manager to get hands-on with our affiliate portfolio and grow it. You'll work directly with some of the biggest publishers in the world, and your work will show up in the numbers — fast.

You'll work across two areas: driving more revenue out of affiliate sites that are already live, and helping take brand-new sites from a blank page to go-live — keyword clustering, content structure, stakeholder coordination, the whole build. Every Google update, every new market, every publisher conversation is something you'll get your hands on.

At WLX, SEO isn't a support function — it's a driving force. We have the resources, the management backing, and the hands-on expertise to make things happen. And unlike an agency, everything we build is ours: our own projects, run in close collaboration with the world's biggest publishers. That means real ownership, real impact, and no client briefs.

This is what you'll do

  • Drive revenue growth on existing affiliate sites: Develop and implement long-term SEO strategies, and own the on-page and off-page work that moves the needle.
  • Improve and maintain rankings on key money pages: Run content audits, apply intent mapping, and improve CTR and SERP feature capture on your highest-value pages.
  • Lead backlink campaigns: Build and execute link-building strategies across multiple affiliate sites, working with agencies, forums, and outreach partners to strengthen domain authority.
  • Help take new affiliate sites live: Own keyword clustering, topic mapping, and content structure based on market and competitor research, and coordinate with stakeholders to get new sites launched from scratch.
  • React fast when the landscape shifts: Assess the impact of Google algorithm updates, figure out what happened and why, and put a clear plan in place to recover traffic — without getting stuck in the noise.

This is what you’ve got

  • Extensive SEO experience, with strong, hands-on expertise in both on-page and off-page work, and a track record of driving organic growth at scale.
  • Fluent in German and English, confident in operating with stakeholders in both languages.
  • Strong analytical thinking and prioritisation skills — you know what moves the needle and can back your decisions with data.
  • Proactive and self-motivated, comfortable owning your workstream without needing to be told what's next.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, flat, startup-style environment.
  • Experience in iGaming or other affiliate marketing industries is a plus.

AI & Data Engineer

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We're looking for a polyglot engineer who is comfortable across the data stack. This is someone who can build AI-powered tools and data infrastructure that make our platform smarter, our people more effective, and our operations more scalable.

This is not a research role. You'll build real systems that people use every day — Slack bots that investigate production incidents, data pipelines that surface anomalies before clients notice them, and AI agents that turn hours of manual trawling into seconds of guided investigation. You'll work across the full stack: Python and TypeScript for AI tooling and integrations, Go for backend services, and SQL for data analysis and pipeline work.

The person we're looking for ships working software, cares about making people's lives easier, and is energised by the pace of the AI landscape. You don't need to have built LLM applications before — but you should be curious, practical, and comfortable learning fast.

You'll work closely with our TechOps, Connectivity, and Data teams to understand their workflows, pain points, and knowledge gaps — then build the tools and infrastructure that solve them. This is a high-leverage role: the systems you build will multiply the effectiveness of every engineer and operator in the company.

What You'll Work On

  • AI-powered investigation tools — Slack-based bots and agents that automatically analyse support tickets, query production logs, and surface relevant context for incident response

  • MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers — authenticated access to ClickHouse, Kubernetes, Atlassian, and GitHub, enabling AI agents to interact with real systems safely

  • Data infrastructure — ClickHouse analytics pipelines, real-time anomaly detection, and platform health monitoring (our "Radar" initiative)

  • AI agent development — constrained, repeatable diagnosis agents that follow investigation playbooks, produce structured outputs, and operate with appropriate guardrails

  • Knowledge engineering — building and curating the corpus that makes our AI tools accurate: documentation, training material, structured metadata, and feedback loops

  • Internal tooling — full-stack applications that bridge the gap between data, AI, and the people who need answers

What We Need

Technical:

  • Strong Python — your primary language for AI tooling, data pipelines, and backend services

  • Systems design – you have extensive experience building data-intensive systems. You can consider tradeoffs and manage system complexity

  • TypeScript / JavaScript — for Slack integrations, web interfaces, and full-stack tooling

  • Go experience is a bonus — we use Go extensively for backend services and CLI tooling

  • SQL — comfortable writing analytical queries against large datasets (ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, or similar)

  • Familiarity with LLM APIs and tooling — Claude, OpenAI, or similar; prompt engineering, function calling, tool use

  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS — your tools will run in production infrastructure

  • Git and Linux fundamentals

  • Experience in financial services is a plus but not essential — domain knowledge can be learned; engineering instinct cannot

How you work:

  • You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate quickly, you get things in front of users, you improve based on feedback

  • You bridge domains. You're comfortable moving between AI, data, infrastructure, and product. You don't wait for someone else to define the interface — you go and understand the problem yourself

  • You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You monitor it, you fix it, you make it better

  • You write things down. Documentation is how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. Good documentation also makes our AI tools better — every well-written page becomes training material

  • You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication is essential

  • You embrace AI as a tool. You use AI to amplify your own productivity — and you build tools that do the same for others

What You Get

  • Growth — this role sits at the intersection of AI, data, and platform engineering. As the company scales, so does the opportunity. This is a new pod with an exciting remit

  • Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

  • Greenfield AI work — you're not maintaining legacy systems; you're building the next generation of intelligent tooling for a trading platform

  • Real impact — the tools you build will be used daily by engineers, operators, and eventually clients. This is not a side project

  • An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

  • Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our people

  • Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Technical Interview with a member of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session. ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Leadership Conversation with our CTO
Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

How to Apply

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

jobs.title: Senior CRM Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Du baust als erste CRM-Person das Retention-Ressort einer Supplement-Marke mit über 200.000 Kund:innen auf — von null, mit eigenem Budget und Tool-Stack.

Über 200.000 Menschen haben bei Wehle Sports, eine Marke der Supplement Hub Gruppe, schon bestellt. Die Marke wächst im Direktgeschäft um rund 60 % pro Jahr — getragen vor allem von der Neukundengewinnung. Was nach dem ersten Kauf passiert, wurde bisher über Agenturen gesteuert. Genau dort liegt der nächste große Hebel: Die ersten 90 Tage nach dem Erstkauf entscheiden, ob aus Kund:innen Stammkund:innen werden.

Dafür gibt es diese Rolle. Du bist die erste CRM-Person im Haus und baust das Ressort von null auf: Lifecycle-Flows, E-Mail, SMS und WhatsApp, ein Loyalty-Programm, das bestehende Abo. Wehle Sports soll im DTC wachsen — CRM ist dafür neben der Neukundengewinnung der zweite große Hebel.

Und du baust nicht nur für eine Marke. Die Supplement Hub Gruppe vereint sieben Marken mit über 500 Produkten und rund 50–60 Mio. € Umsatz. Was bei Wehle funktioniert, wird zum Playbook für die ganze Gruppe — und aus der ersten CRM-Rolle wird in zwei bis drei Jahren die Leitung eines gruppenweiten CRM-Teams.

Warum es diese Rolle gibt

Wehle Sports ist über starke Produkte und Neukundengewinnung groß geworden. E-Mail, SMS und ein Abo-Programm gibt es — aber es gibt kein CRM-Team, keinen eigenen Tool-Stack über Klaviyo hinaus und keine durchgängige Logik, die Erstkäufer:innen systematisch zum zweiten und dritten Kauf führt. Bisher lag das bei Agenturen.

Das ändert sich jetzt. Das DTC-Team wird gerade neu aufgebaut. Retention soll so schnell wie sinnvoll ins Haus, eine Agentur bleibt nur dort, wo sie nachweislich mehr bringt. Dafür braucht es jemanden, der kein fertiges System verwaltet, sondern das erste baut.

Was du bewegen wirst

Nicht als Aufgabenliste, sondern als das, was in zwölf Monaten anders sein soll:

  • Die ersten 90 Tage sind gebaut. Welcome, Post-Purchase, Replenishment, Cross-Sell, Winback und Abandonment-Flows laufen, sind getestet und führen Neukund:innen gezielt zum Wiederkauf und zu passenden Produkten rund um Gelenkgesundheit.

  • Die Kanäle spielen zusammen. E-Mail, SMS und WhatsApp sind ein Lifecycle statt drei Silos — und WhatsApp ist ein eigener Retention-Kanal mit eigener Liste.

  • Loyalty ist live, das Abo wächst. Du hast ein Loyalty-Programm ausgewählt, gebaut und gelauncht und das Abo-Programm bei Quote, Churn und Kündigungsstrecken weiterentwickelt.

  • Die Zahlen sind deine. Segmentierung und Kohorten-Reporting zu Retention, CLV und CLV:CAC stehen — und du steuerst das Ressort danach, nicht nach Öffnungsraten.

  • Das Ressort steht. Tool-Stack, CRM-Budget und Insourcing-Plan sind entschieden — von dir, mit Business Case. Die Prozesse sind so dokumentiert, dass sie auf die nächste Marke übertragbar sind.

Wie hier gearbeitet wird

Supplement Hub ist effizienzgetrieben: Calls gibt es, wenn sie nötig sind, Entscheidungen fallen in Tagen. Neue Produkte sind in zwei bis drei Wochen von der Idee im Lager — wenn dein Cross-Sell ein Produkt braucht, ist das kein Jahresprojekt.

  • Du entscheidest über Tools und Budget. Freigaben brauchst du nur, wenn du über das gemeinsam vereinbarte Budget hinausgehst.

  • Am Anfang baust und verschickst du selbst — es gibt noch kein Team, das umsetzt. Das Team entsteht mit dir.

  • Testen ist ausdrücklich gewollt: neue Kanäle, Angebote und Mechaniken ausprobieren, messen, skalieren oder stoppen. Fehler sind erlaubt, wenn sie gemessen werden.

  • Das Team arbeitet remote im DACH-Raum und trifft sich regelmäßig zu Team-Events und Workations in Berlin.

Wen wir suchen

Wir suchen keinen perfekten Lebenslauf, sondern einen Nachweis: Du hast Kund:innen einer Consumer-Marke schon einmal messbar zum Wiederkauf gebracht.

Das brauchst du auf jeden Fall

  • Rund fünf Jahre CRM- oder Retention-Erfahrung bei einer B2C-Marke im Consumer-Goods- oder D2C-E-Commerce-Umfeld — etwa Supplements, Food, Beauty oder Skincare.

  • Du kannst an Zahlen zeigen, dass du Wiederkaufrate oder CLV gesteigert hast — idealerweise auf Kohortenebene.

  • Ein B2C-CRM-Tool beherrschst du auf Expertenniveau: Flows, Segmente und Reporting hast du selbst gebaut, nicht nur gebrieft.

  • Du setzt selbst um. Konzepte schreiben reicht hier am Anfang nicht — du baust und verschickst, bis es ein Team gibt.

  • Kohortenanalysen in Sheets, Excel oder einem BI-Tool sind für dich Alltag.

  • Fließendes Deutsch in Wort und Schrift, weil du für deutschsprachige Kund:innen schreibst.

Das ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Erfahrung mit Nahrungsergänzungsmitteln und Health Claims

  • Klaviyo und Shopify Plus im Tagesgeschäft

  • Abo-Modelle: Churn, Pausen- und Kündigungsstrecken gesteuert

  • Ein Loyalty-Programm oder einen WhatsApp-Kanal aufgebaut

  • Schon einmal einen CRM-Bereich von null aufgebaut oder Agenturthemen ins Haus geholt

Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt, bist aber sicher, die Lücke schnell zu schließen? Dann melde dich.

Die Vorteile für dich

  • Ein weißes Blatt mit voller Hoheit. Tool-Stack (außer Klaviyo und Shopify Plus), CRM-Budget und Struktur entscheidest du.

  • Ein Mentor als Chef. Du berichtest an einen Head of DTC, der eine D2C-Marke vom sieben- in den achtstelligen Bereich mitskaliert hat.

  • Ein Weg nach oben, der real ist. Funktioniert der Aufbau, führst du in zwei bis drei Jahren ein eigenes CRM-Team für die ganze Gruppe.

  • Ein Bonus, der an deiner Wirkung hängt — gemessen an der CLV-Entwicklung deiner Kundenkohorten.

  • Rückenwind statt Rechtfertigungsdruck. Eine finanzstarke Gruppe mit sieben Marken, über 200.000 Kund:innen bei Wehle und ein DTC-Geschäft, das um rund 60 % pro Jahr wächst.

  • 100 % Remote in der DACH-Zeitzone, mit regelmäßigen Team-Events und Workations in Berlin.

Warum du dich jetzt melden solltest

Selten findest du eine Marke, bei der Produkt, Nachfrage und 200.000 Kund:innen schon da sind — und nur die Retention fehlt. Genau da steht Wehle Sports heute. Wenn du CRM nicht verwalten, sondern einmal richtig aufbauen willst, ist das dein Zeitpunkt.

jobs.description:
About RhymeQ

RhymeQ is on a mission to make quantum programmable for every developer. Today, developing quantum software often requires deep physics expertise and code tailored to specific hardware. We’re removing these barriers so developers can focus on solving problems.

Headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, we bring together an international team with an open mindset, an energetic team spirit, and a shared drive to build something that matters. We value initiative, ownership, and collaboration, giving everyone the space to contribute ideas, take responsibility, and help shape the future of quantum programming.

Your role

As our Developer Community Lead, you will help developers discover, write their first quantum program, and keep building. Your goal is to turn early interest into an active community where developers learn from one another, share projects, and contribute to the product’s development.

You will combine technical education, community building, and developer outreach. Working closely with our founders and engineering team, you will shape the community experience and grow the community internationally to our target size.

What you will do

  • Grow an active developer community: Build relationships with universities, programming communities, quantum organizations, and event organizers to attract developers to RHYME.
  • Help newcomers succeed: Create a clear onboarding journey, from registration and installation to running and sharing a first quantum program.
  • Build reasons to return: Organize onboarding cohorts, office hours, coding challenges, and hackathons that encourage continued learning and participation.
  • Create useful technical content: Develop tutorials, sample projects, livestreams, posts, and talks that make quantum programming approachable.
  • Support community contributions: Encourage developers to share their work, answer questions, and help others. Identify and support potential community ambassadors.
  • Connect developers with the product team: Turn questions, feedback, and recurring problems into clear recommendations for the compiler, tooling, and documentation.
  • Measure what works: Track acquisition, activation, retention, and contributions, and use the results to improve community programs.

What you bring

  • Bachelor’s in computer science, PhD is preferred.
  • Over 2 years of experience growing a developer community for a technical product, with results you can demonstrate through active users, downloads, contributors, event participation, or other relevant measures.
  • Practical Python skills. You can run code examples, lead a live tutorial, and help a newcomer troubleshoot their setup.
  • The ability to explain technical concepts clearly and make learning engaging, whether in writing, on camera, or on stage.
  • Strong written and spoken English and confidence working with an international audience.
  • A self-driven approach: you can set priorities, organize programs, deliver them, and learn from the results.
  • An open, supportive communication style that helps developers feel comfortable asking questions and sharing unfinished work.
  • An understanding of quantum computing fundamentals, or the motivation to learn them quickly.

Your ability to build trust with developers, teach through code, and grow sustained participation matters most.

What we offer

  • Ownership from the start: Shape our community strategy, programs, and developer experience as our first community hire.
  • Direct collaboration with the founders: Work closely with the people building RHYME and bring developer needs into product decisions.
  • An open, international team: Share ideas, experiment, and learn alongside colleagues who value initiative and collaboration.
  • Visible impact: Help developers move from curiosity about quantum computing to building their own applications.
  • Remote work within Europe.
